Paragraph 1 — Brief summary
Improving rest involves establishing consistent habits and environmental factors that support sleep quality. This includes regular sleep-wake times, a relaxing pre-sleep routine, and a comfortable sleep environment.

Paragraph 2 — Practical steps
- Schedule: Go to bed and wake up at the same times daily to regulate your circadian rhythm.
- Wind-down routine: Spend 30–60 minutes before bed on calming activities (reading, gentle stretching, deep-breathing).
- Environment: Keep the bedroom dark, cool (around 18–20°C / 65–68°F), and quiet. Use blackout curtains or a white-noise machine if needed.
- Limit stimulants: Avoid caffeine and heavy meals within 4–6 hours of bedtime. Reduce screen time in the hour before bed or use blue-light filters.
- Daytime habits: Get exposure to daylight and include regular physical activity (but avoid intense exercise close to bedtime).

Paragraph 3 — When to seek help
If sleep problems persist despite good habits (trouble falling asleep, waking frequently, daytime sleepiness), consult a healthcare provider. They can check for underlying causes (sleep apnea, restless legs, mood disorders) and recommend treatments such as cognitive-behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I).

- Create a 30-minute pre-sleep routine.
- Keep bedroom cool, dark, and quiet.
- Avoid caffeine after midday.
- Get at least 20 minutes of morning sunlight.
Track your sleep quality each morning and note changes.
